Through VS Code I use development tools, extensions, or resources (many of which are via the autonomous assistance of my GitHub Copilot Chat in 'Agent' mode but also sometimes manually), which is mostly revolving around  maintaining/committing/publishing on GitHub.com repositories AND creating and generating lots of my project documentation artifacts/user guides/.html files/markdown files about my project or content.

PART #2:   I do smaller chunk of my work (about 10% to 15%) on my various projects creating secondary content & sub-components which are related to my various primary PowerApp/PowerAutomate/SharePoint list projects. I also do quite a bit of work with various Microsoft/M365/Office suite software (like Snipping Tool, Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, & Edge).

PART 3:    I do the smallest chunk of my work (about 5% to 10%) with smaller tools or software as tertiary activities or just as needed during the development, testing, release/publication, post-release, and long-term maintenance of my various projects. This can include things like using Notepad++, Adobe Acrobat Pro, Microsoft PowerToys, MS PowerPoint, MS Edge, PowerShell 7, MS OneNote, writing T-SQL queries and stored procedures (using both 'Azure Data Studio' and 'SSMS', to both pull & transform large bulk data/information from my organization's many nation-wide databases), as well as creating and using VBA macros/python/.bat/deep-linked URLs/etc. during development in within both my IDE and local machine environments.
